title: STS shortcuts and their IntelliJ workflow equivalents
answer: STS is based on the Eclipse platform, so common STS/Eclipse shortcuts include Ctrl+Shift+R for Open Resource, Ctrl+Shift+T for Open Type, Ctrl+O for Quick Outline, F3 for Open Declaration, Ctrl+Shift+G for references, Ctrl+Space for content assist, Ctrl+1 for Quick Fix, Ctrl+Shift+F for formatting, and Alt+Shift+R for Rename. Exact bindings can vary by operating system or customized keymap. In this AeroTopo course the Java IDE is IntelliJ IDEA only, so the lesson demonstrates the equivalent navigation, completion, intention, formatting, and refactoring workflows in IntelliJ rather than switching the simulator to STS.

steps.question: STS commonly uses Ctrl+Shift+R to open a resource by name when you know the file but not its exact package location. In an IntelliJ-only AeroTopo workflow, how does Go to File provide the same navigation idea without manually expanding the project tree?
steps.why: Both workflows solve the same developer problem: file-name-driven navigation. This course remains IntelliJ-only, so we demonstrate the equivalent action without switching IDEs.

steps.title: Map STS Rename to IntelliJ safe refactoring
steps.question: Semantic rename uses the IDE symbol model and is safer than replacing matching text blindly across unrelated files or comments. STS/Eclipse commonly uses Alt+Shift+R for Rename so a Java symbol is changed semantically across its references rather than through unsafe text replacement. Why is IntelliJ's safe Rename refactoring the correct equivalent to remember for production code changes?
steps.why: Semantic rename uses the IDE symbol model and is safer than replacing matching text blindly across unrelated files or comments.
